context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and the US. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and low-bandwidth availability.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Primary Users)
- Regulatory & Compliance Auditors (External Users)
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform (Central Software System spanning GCP regions)
- Regional API Gateways and Application Services (GCP Cloud Run / GKE containers)
- Regional Datastores and Audit Logging Services (GCP Cloud SQL and Cloud Logging)
- Native AI Inference Service (GCP Vertex AI)
- Video/Media Gateways (WebRTC SFU / LiveKit)
- External Pharmacy Networks, National Identity Providers, and Payment Gateways

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians -> Regional API Gateways via HTTPS and WebRTC
- Telehealth Platform -> External Pharmacy Networks via REST and HL7 FHIR APIs
- Telehealth Platform -> National Identity Providers via OIDC/SAML
- Telehealth Platform -> Payment & Insurance Providers via HTTPS
- Inter-container communication via gRPC and internal REST within GCP regions

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider:** Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` (Frankfurt) and `us-central1` (Iowa) for data residency
- **Compute:** GCP Cloud Run and GKE for scalable regional microservices
- **Database & Storage:** GCP Cloud SQL for isolated regional patient datastores
- **AI & Analytics:** GCP Vertex AI for regionally hosted, traceable medical AI inference
- **Media Streaming:** WebRTC with STUN/TURN fallback for rural, low-bandwidth connections (<300 kbit/s)
- **Interoperability:** HL7 FHIR (US) and national e-prescription standards (EU)

## Rationale
Partitioning infrastructure across isolated GCP regions guarantees compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR data residency mandates. Native AI and adaptive WebRTC streaming satisfy stringent traceability and low-bandwidth availability requirements.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Web & Mobile Apps using React / React Native)
- Google Cloud API Gateway with Open Policy Agent (OPA)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Video Streaming Service (mediasoup SFU on GCP Compute Engine with TURN/STUN relay)
- Integration Service (Node.js)
- Datastores (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Memorystore Redis, Google Cloud BigQuery / Cloud Storage)
- Regional Deployments (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians to API Gateway via HTTPS, WSS, and WebRTC/UDP
- API Gateway to Core Telehealth & AI Services via internal gRPC
- AI Symptom Checker to Audit Log Store via Google Cloud Pub/Sub
- Integration Service to external pharmacy networks via national standards and HL7 FHIR
- Cross-region access between gateways via federated mTLS over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional isolation and data residency
- Go: Powers the Core Telehealth Service for reliable business logic execution
- Python / FastAPI: Runs inference for the AI Symptom Checker Service
- WebRTC / mediasoup & TURN/STUN: Handles video streaming and rural low-bandwidth connections (<300 kbit/s)
- Open Policy Agent (OPA): Evaluates dynamic, purpose-based patient consent policies
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Memorystore Redis: Provides region-isolated transactional and cache storage
- Google Cloud BigQuery / Cloud Storage: Maintains immutable audit logs for AI traceability

## Rationale
Isolated regional deployments in GCP ensure patient data remains within its source jurisdiction to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA. Asynchronous messaging via Cloud Pub/Sub and resilient WebRTC streaming maintain high availability and performance even over unstable rural internet connections.

Web & Mobile Apps.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for unstable rural connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- Web & Mobile Apps Container (React / React Native)
- UI Presentation Layer (Component)
- Video/Audio Session Controller (Component)
- Offline Data Synchronizer (Component)
- Regional Configuration & Telemetry Manager (Component)
- Local Consent & State Manager (Component)
- Google Cloud API Gateway with Open Policy Agent (OPA)
- Video Streaming Service (mediasoup SFU on GCP Compute Engine)

## Relationships
- UI Presentation Layer -> Regional Configuration & Telemetry Manager [Local JS Calls]
- UI Presentation Layer -> Local Consent & State Manager [Local JS Calls]
- UI Presentation Layer -> Offline Data Synchronizer [Local JS Calls]
- Video/Audio Session Controller -> Video Streaming Service [WebRTC/UDP, failing over to TCP/TURN relay via API Gateway]
- Regional Configuration & Telemetry Manager & UI Presentation Layer -> Google Cloud API Gateway with OPA [mTLS / HTTPS / WSS with regional headers]
- Local Consent & State Manager -> Offline Data Synchronizer [Local JS Calls]

## Technology Stack
- React / React Native: Cross-platform UI development for web and mobile devices.
- IndexedDB and SQLite: Local storage for offline data caching and consent persistence.
- WebRTC, STUN/TURN, and mediasoup SFU: Real-time video/audio streaming with adaptive bitrate and fallback support.
- Google Cloud API Gateway with OPA: Secured API routing and policy enforcement across regions (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`).

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance by pinning client requests and data processing to regional GCP datacenters. Additionally, client-side consent management, offline synchronization, and adaptive WebRTC fallbacks guarantee reliable, compliant telehealth services even over unstable rural internet connections.

Google Cloud API Gateway with OPA.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It runs on GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) ensuring strict regional data residency and regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- Web & Mobile Apps (React / React Native)
- Google Cloud API Gateway with OPA (Google Cloud API Gateway, Open Policy Agent)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Video Streaming Service (mediasoup SFU on GCP Compute Engine)
- Integration Service (Node.js)
- Datastores (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Memorystore Redis, Google Cloud BigQuery, Cloud Storage)
- API Gateway Components: API Router, Context Extractor, Rate Limiting Component, Authorization Engine (OPA), Audit Logger (Fluentbit sidecar)

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Apps -> Google Cloud API Gateway with OPA: Sends requests and media [HTTPS, WSS, WebRTC/UDP]
- API Router -> Rate Limiting Component: Checks quotas [gRPC / Memorystore Redis]
- API Router -> Context Extractor: Passes raw requests [In-memory]
- Context Extractor -> Authorization Engine (OPA): Forwards claims [gRPC]
- Authorization Engine -> Audit Logger: Emits decision logs [Async IPC / Fluentd]
- Google Cloud API Gateway -> Backend Services (Core/AI/Integration): Routes traffic [gRPC with JWT/Token propagation]
- Google Cloud API Gateway -> Google Cloud API Gateway: Cross-region access [Federated mTLS over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider for regional isolation in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`
- Open Policy Agent (OPA): Enforces dynamic purpose-based patient consent via Rego policies
- Google Cloud API Gateway: Manages API routing, TLS termination, and mTLS enforcement
- Memorystore Redis: Backs the rate-limiting component for traffic throttling
- Fluentbit: Sidecar component for forwarding structured audit logs to BigQuery

## Rationale
This architecture enforces GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints by isolating processing per region while allowing secure, consented cross-region access. The component breakdown within the API gateway ensures low-latency authorization, auditability, and resilient routing for unstable connections.

Core Telehealth Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and robust performance on unstable rural internet connections.

## Key Elements
- **Consultation Manager (Go)**: Orchestrates video session lifecycles.
- **Prescription Engine (Go)**: Manages regional e-prescription routing.
- **Consent & Policy Enforcement Engine (Go)**: Enforces region-specific data residency and explicit patient consents.
- **Audit Logger (Go)**: Emits structured audit trails.
- **Symptom Checker Orchestrator (Go)**: Coordinates AI triage assessments and model versioning.
- **Degraded Mode Handler (Go)**: Adapts network quality for low-bandwidth connections.
- **Video Streaming Service**: mediasoup SFU on GCP Compute Engine with TURN/STUN relay.
- **Datastores**: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Memorystore Redis, and Google Cloud BigQuery.

## Relationships
- **Consent & Policy Enforcement Engine** -> **Datastores**: Executes region-isolated queries [PostgreSQL and Redis protocols].
- **Consultation Manager** -> **Video Streaming Service**: Controls media sessions [gRPC].
- **Symptom Checker Orchestrator** -> **AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)**: Triggers triage analysis [gRPC].
- **Prescription Engine** -> **Integration Service (Node.js)**: Dispatches regional e-prescription payloads [gRPC].
- **Internal Components** -> **Audit Logger**: Dispatches immutable tracing payloads [Buffered Go Channels].

## Technology Stack
- **Go**: Chosen for high performance and concurrency in core telehealth orchestration.
- **Python / FastAPI**: Used for the AI Symptom Checker Service to leverage machine learning ecosystem libraries.
- **mediasoup SFU on GCP Compute Engine**: Selected for scalable, low-latency video streaming.
- **Google Cloud API Gateway with Open Policy Agent (OPA)**: Implemented for secure, policy-driven API routing.
- **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Memorystore Redis**: Utilized for transactional data storage and caching with strict regional isolation.

## Rationale
This architecture uses GCP multi-region deployment (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) with isolated datastores to satisfy strict GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates. The modular Go component design within the Core Telehealth Service ensures high availability, medical device traceability, and graceful degradation for rural connections under 300 kbit/s.

AI Symptom Checker Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US while enforcing strict regional data residency. The AI Symptom Checker Service is architected as an isolated, compliant component pipeline running locally on GCP to meet GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR standards.

## Key Elements
- **API Router / Endpoint Controller**: FastAPI-based controller validating incoming gRPC requests.
- **Consent & Policy Enforcement Interceptor**: FastAPI Middleware verifying active patient consent per data-sharing purpose.
- **Regional Context & Guardrails Engine**: Enforces clinical triage guidelines and strips PHI prior to inference.
- **Inference Orchestrator**: Manages prompt engineering, context windows, and model execution.
- **ML Model Runtime**: Runs local quantized LLM/classification models via ONNX Runtime / gRPC-local.
- **Clinical Triage Validator**: Post-processes urgency scores against deterministic safety thresholds.
- **Audit & Traceability Logger**: Captures inputs, model versions, and outputs for EU MDR traceability.

## Relationships
- *API Router* -> *Consent Interceptor* (In-process FastAPI Middleware)
- *Consent Interceptor* -> *Guardrails Engine* (In-process)
- *Guardrails Engine* -> *Inference Orchestrator* (In-process)
- *Inference Orchestrator* -> *ML Model Runtime* (In-process via ONNX Runtime / gRPC-local)
- *Inference Orchestrator* -> *Clinical Triage Validator* (In-process)
- *Clinical Triage Validator* -> *API Router* (In-process)
- *Audit Logger* -> *Google Cloud Pub/Sub* ([gRPC])
- *Audit Logger* -> *Google Cloud BigQuery / Cloud Storage* ([REST/gRPC via Pub/Sub])

## Technology Stack
- **Python / FastAPI**: Core framework for the AI Symptom Checker container due to robust ML ecosystem support.
- **ONNX Runtime / vLLM**: Local model runtime executing quantized LLMs to prevent external API calls and ensure regional data residency.
- **Google Cloud Pub/Sub & BigQuery / Cloud Storage**: Asynchronous messaging and regional datastores ensuring immutable audit logging for EU MDR compliance.
- **GCP (europe-west3, us-central1)**: Target cloud regions enforcing isolated data storage per jurisdiction.

## Rationale
This component architecture separates boundary security, deterministic validation, and local inference to comply with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR regulations. Asynchronous, region-locked telemetry and in-process execution eliminate cross-border data leakage while maintaining high accountability and availability.

Video Streaming Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Video Streaming Service container provides low-latency WebRTC video consultations for the Cross-Border Telehealth Platform across EU and US regions. It ensures robust communication for rural patients with unstable internet connections while maintaining strict regional data residency.]

## Key Elements
- Signaling Server (Node.js / WebSockets)
- SFU Router Core (mediasoup / C++ / Node.js)
- Adaptive Bitrate & Quality Manager (Go)
- TURN/STUN Relay Manager (Coturn on GCP Compute Engine)
- Media Session Audit Logger (Go)
- Geo-Distributed TURN Coordinator (Go)

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Apps -> Signaling Server: Session control [WSS]
- Web & Mobile Apps <-> SFU Router Core: Media streaming [WebRTC/UDP/DTLS]
- Adaptive Bitrate & Quality Manager -> SFU Router Core: Adjusts simulcast layers [Internal IPC]
- SFU Router Core -> Media Session Audit Logger: Emits session telemetry [gRPC]
- Web & Mobile Apps -> Geo-Distributed TURN Coordinator: Relay allocation [HTTPS]
- Geo-Distributed TURN Coordinator -> TURN/STUN Relay Manager: Provisions endpoints [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- mediasoup SFU: Minimizes CPU and bandwidth overhead for video routing
- Coturn on GCP Compute Engine: Handles NAT traversal for unstable rural connections
- Node.js & Go: Delivers high-concurrency connection management and telemetry processing

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces regional data residency by isolating session metadata locally within europe-west3 and us-central1. It guarantees degraded-mode operation below 300 kbit/s via dynamic bitrate management.]

Integration Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and AI symptom checking for patients across the EU and US. The Integration Service securely bridges internal domain models with external pharmacy networks while strictly enforcing regional data residency.

## Key Elements
- FHIR Adapter Component (TypeScript / HAPI FHIR or custom mapper)
- EU E-Prescription Gateway Component (TypeScript)
- Data Residency Enforcer Component (Region-isolated instances in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- Audit Logger Component
- Retry & Dead-Letter Queue Component (BullMQ / Redis)
- Transformation Engine Component (JSONata / Handlebars)
- Circuit Breaker & Rate Limiter Component (Opossum)

## Relationships
- Integration Service (EU/US instances) -> External Pharmacy Networks: Transmits payloads [HTTPS/REST, mTLS]
- EU E-Prescription Gateway & FHIR Adapter -> Transformation Engine: Applies schema mappings [In-memory]
- Adapters -> Retry & Dead-Letter Queue: Offloads failed outbound requests [Redis protocol]
- Adapters -> Circuit Breaker: Evaluates health and dispatches outbound requests [In-memory]
- Circuit Breaker -> External Pharmacy Networks: Sends payloads [HTTPS/REST, mTLS]
- Integration Service -> Google Cloud BigQuery: Records audit logs asynchronously [BigQuery API]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js with TypeScript: Ensures rapid asynchronous I/O handling and strict type safety for healthcare schemas.
- Redis (Memorystore) via BullMQ: Provides reliable, low-latency job persistence for asynchronous message queuing.
- JSONata: Enables declarative, side-effect-free data transformation for complex national e-prescription schemas.
- Opossum: Delivers lightweight, in-memory circuit breaking and rate limiting for external pharmacy integrations.

## Rationale
This component architecture enforces strict regional data residency by isolating EU and US traffic paths to comply with GDPR and HIPAA. Furthermore, it guarantees resilience against unstable rural internet connections through robust queuing, schema transformation, and circuit-breaking mechanisms.

Datastores.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform is a secure telemedicine system providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability under unstable network conditions.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Web & Mobile Apps)
- Regulatory and Compliance Auditors
- External Pharmacy Networks, National Identity Providers, Payment & Insurance Providers
- Google Cloud API Gateway with Open Policy Agent (OPA)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (Python / FastAPI)
- Video Streaming Service (mediasoup SFU on GCP Compute Engine, TURN/STUN relay)
- Integration Service (Node.js)
- Datastores Container components: Regional Transactional DB (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL), Caching Layer (Memorystore Redis), Audit & Analytics Store (Google Cloud BigQuery), Document Store / FHIR Repository (Google Cloud Storage), Encryption Key Management Component (Google Cloud KMS), CDC & Event Ingestion Pipeline (Google Cloud Pub/Sub & Dataflow), Data Masking & Tokenization Component, Database Connection Pooling (PgBouncer)

## Relationships
- Web & Mobile Apps -> Google Cloud API Gateway: API requests and video streaming [HTTPS and WebRTC over UDP/TCP]
- Core Telehealth Service -> Regional Transactional DB & Caching Layer via Database Connection Pooling: Relational reads/writes and session management [PostgreSQL and Redis protocols over TLS]
- AI Symptom Checker Service -> Audit & Analytics Store: Immutable AI traceability logging [HTTPS / BigQuery insert APIs]
- Integration Service -> Document Store & Regional Transactional DB: FHIR resources and e-prescriptions [HTTPS and PostgreSQL protocol]
- Regional Transactional DB, Document Store, & Audit Store -> Encryption Key Management Component: Data-at-rest encryption [gRPC over TLS with IAM]
- Regional Transactional DB -> CDC & Event Ingestion Pipeline: Change data capture streams [Google Cloud Pub/Sub native protocol over TLS]
- Integration Service & CDC Pipeline -> Data Masking & Tokenization Component: PHI/PII sanitization [Internal gRPC]
- Audit Store -> Regulatory Auditors: Compliance reporting [BigQuery SQL via IAM-secured HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider utilizing regions europe-west3 and us-central1 for regional isolation.
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL with PgBouncer: Relational database and connection pooling for transactional data and resilience against network flapping.
- Memorystore Redis: In-memory cache for low-latency session management and temporary state.
- Google Cloud BigQuery & Cloud Storage: Analytics, immutable audit logging, and FHIR document storage.
- Google Cloud KMS: Customer-managed encryption keys for strict cryptographic data isolation.
- Google Cloud Pub/Sub & Dataflow: Asynchronous event ingestion pipeline for zero-loss telemetry logging.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional isolation between europe-west3 and us-central1 to guarantee GDPR and HIPAA compliance while keeping EU health data strictly within the EU. Furthermore, it incorporates robust connection pooling, encrypted key management, and decoupled audit logging to meet high availability, security, and EU MDR traceability mandates.
